# Tooling

Read these rules, and then NR-19, before you add a script, a tsconfig, a format or lint config, or a Foundry project. This page holds the full text of the live rules of the group, from [README.md](../README.md).

## NR-06: Every tsconfig path exists `[GAP]`

> Every literal local path named by an owned tsconfig exists.

Old number: 2.1.5.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check tsconfig-paths`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: ownedTsconfigs reads the `.` root's own folder without recursion and then only members and non-packages (tsconfig-paths.ts:114-116). A tsconfig directly in a cluster root, for example hardhat/v3/tsconfig.json with `"include": ["./deleted"]`, is skipped (kind workspace-root, member=false); so is a tsconfig in a root-owned subfolder such as scripts/tsconfig.json. fhevm-npm/tsconfig.json is outside the inventory and is not read either. Fix: issue I-73.

Issues: I-73.

`include`, `exclude`, `files`,
`references[].path` and relative `extends` entries are checked in root, member and non-package tsconfigs; globs are
not literal claims, and conventional transient-output names (`node_modules`, `out`, `cache`, …) may be absent.

```jsonc
// ✅ Existing source path and a glob that may currently match nothing.
{ "include": ["./src", "./generated/**/*.ts"] }

// ❌ A deleted literal path silently weakens TypeScript's coverage.
{ "exclude": ["./test/deleted-file.ts"] }
```

## NR-14: Match the tsc mode to the tsconfig shape `[GAP]`

> A `tsc` invocation matches its tsconfig's shape.

Old number: 2.1.13.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check tsc-mode`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: Three changes pass. (1) Bare tsc with a valued flag: "lint": "tsc --noEmit --pretty false" on a solution-style ./tsconfig.json; the positional `false` makes the parser skip the invocation (tsc-mode.ts:121). (2) Inheritance: "lint": "tsc -p ./tsconfig.lint.json --noEmit" where tsconfig.lint.json is `{ "extends": "./tsconfig.json", "references": [...] }` and ./tsconfig.json has "files": []; isSolutionStyle reads the raw file, sees no `files`, and passes, while tsc inherits the empty `files` and checks nothing. (3) A path-qualified binary, `./node_modules/.bin/tsc -p ...`: the token is not `tsc` (tsc-mode.ts:98). Only package.json scripts of inventoried packages are read; a tsc call in the Makefile, a shell script or fhevm-npm/package.json is not. Fix: issue I-77.

Issues: I-77.

A solution-style tsconfig (empty `files` plus
`references`) must be driven with `tsc -b`: project mode (`tsc -p`, or bare `tsc`) loads it, checks zero files and
exits 0 — the silent failure TS18002 would catch, except `references` suppresses it. Leaves may use either mode.

```jsonc
// ✅ Build mode walks the references of the solution file.
"lint": "tsc -b ./tsconfig.json --noEmit"

// ❌ Project mode on { "files": [], "references": [...] } checks nothing and still passes.
"lint": "tsc -p ./tsconfig.json --noEmit"
```

## NR-29: One Foundry version in the manifest `[GAP]`

> The manifest is the single source of truth for the Foundry version.

Old number: 4.1.2.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check foundry`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: The version is duplicated in .github/workflows/sdk-cleartext-publish-release.yml:69 (`version: v1.5.1`), and that workflow never runs `check foundry`: bumping the manifest and sdk-cleartext-tests.yml to v1.6.0 while leaving the release workflow at v1.5.1 passes, and releases build with the old forge. Fix: issue I-87.

Issues: I-49, I-87.

The repository declares one exact
version in `npm-manifest.json#foundry.version`, compared with `forge --version` by `fhevm-npm check foundry`. Packages must not
duplicate the pin in `.foundry-version` files.

```jsonc
// ✅ One repository-wide pin, checked automatically.
"foundry": { "version": "1.2.3-v1.2.3" }

// ❌ A package-local pin can drift from the repository policy.
some-package/.foundry-version
```

## NR-30: Foundry projects inherit the format policy `[GAP]`

> Every Foundry project inherits the shared formatting policy.

Old number: 4.1.3.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check foundry`

Evidence:

- Gap, wrong check: Compliant change that fails: extends = { path = "../../foundry.base.toml", strategy = "replace-arrays" } in `[profile.default]`. Forge accepts the table form (the installed forge 1.5.1 binary contains the strategies `replace-arrays` and `no-collision`), but the regex at foundry.ts:204 accepts a quoted string only. Any other valid TOML spelling fails too, for example the header `[ profile.default ]`. NR-43c says a Foundry answer comes from `forge config --json`, never from a parsed foundry.toml; this is the one place that parses it. Also loose: only a foundry.toml in an inventoried package's own folder is read (foundry.ts:27-29), so a foundry.toml in a subfolder, without extends, passes. Fix: issue I-88.

Issues: I-01, I-49, I-88.

A package declaring a non-empty `forge:fmt`
script has a `foundry.toml` in the same directory. Every `foundry.toml` declares `[profile.default].extends` for
the workspace root's `foundry.base.toml`; `fhevm-npm check foundry` verifies that ownership and compares every project's effective `[fmt]`
values with the shared file. Package-specific `[fmt].ignore` values are exempt.

The one exception to `extends` is a `standalone` project: the consumer runner copies it out of the workspace and
installs it on its own, so where it runs there is no shared file to extend (forge treats a missing `extends`
target as a hard error). It restates the `[fmt]` policy inline instead, and `fhevm-npm check foundry` still compares its
effective values with the shared file — the exemption is from the mechanism, never from the policy.

```toml
# ✅ Package-local paths and compiler settings remain local; formatting policy is inherited.
[profile.default]
extends = "../../foundry.base.toml"

# ❌ No extends: future changes to the shared formatting policy would not reach this project.
[profile.default]
src = "pkg/src"
```

## NR-43: Common hygiene scripts `[GAP]`

> Private source-owning workspace packages expose common hygiene scripts.

Old number: 5.1.4.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check scripts`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: Keep all required formatting leaves, but change fmt and fmt:check to echo done. Nonempty-script checks pass, while neither formatter runs. Fix: issue I-95.

Issues: I-42, I-95.

Every `dev`, `shared-helper` and
`internal-consumer` package defines non-empty `fmt`, `fmt:check`, `lint`, `prettier:check` and `prettier:write`;
`fmt`/`fmt:check` are the orchestrator's formatting verbs (prettier plus `forge fmt` where the package owns Solidity).
One exception: a package at `<owner>/pkg` whose parent `<owner>` is an inventoried package whose name ends in `-dev`,
such as a workspace-native template, leaves `fmt` and `fmt:check` to that parent, which must define them; it still
defines its own `lint`, `prettier:check` and `prettier:write`. Repository tooling thus stays out of the template users
receive.

```jsonc
// ✅ The package chooses what is covered while exposing the shared entry points.
"scripts": {
  "fmt": "npm run prettier:write && npm run forge:fmt",
  "fmt:check": "npm run prettier:check && npm run forge:fmt:check",
  "lint": "eslint . && tsc --noEmit",
  "prettier:check": "prettier --check .",
  "prettier:write": "prettier --write ."
}

// ✅ A template at <owner>/pkg under a `…-dev` owner: its own lint and Prettier scripts; fmt and fmt:check sit on <owner>.
"scripts": {
  "lint": "npm run lint:ts && npm run prettier:check",
  "lint:ts": "eslint .",
  "prettier:check": "prettier --check .",
  "prettier:write": "prettier --write ."
}

// ❌ An internal consumer with source files but no discoverable formatting checks.
"scripts": { "test": "hardhat test" }
```

## NR-43a: The artifact verb is compile `[GAP]`

> The artifact verb is `compile`; `build` is the optional gated sweep.

Old number: 5.1.4a.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check scripts`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: A `compile` that rewrites a tracked file (e.g. emitting into a committed pkg/ts/index.ts) leaves a dirty tree that no gate in build-ci or ci reports. Fix: issue I-96.

Issues: I-07, I-21, I-96.

Every dev owner of a published payload
defines `compile` (writes only gitignored output, never tracked files). A `build` script on a `dev`, `shared-helper` or
`internal-consumer` package must reach `fmt:check`, `lint` and `compile` through same-package `npm run` references.

```jsonc
// ✅ compile emits artifacts; build gates them behind formatting and lint, in lifecycle order.
"scripts": {
  "build": "npm run fmt:check && npm run lint && npm run compile",
  "compile": "npm run compile:pkg:ts:cjs && npm run compile:pkg:ts:esm"
}

// ❌ A `build` that skips the gates silently redefines the sweep.
"scripts": { "build": "npm run compile" }
```

## NR-43b: Generators expose the full round trip `[GAP]`

> A package that generates exposes the full round trip.

Old number: 5.1.4b.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check scripts`

Evidence:

- Gap, wrong check: Wrong: verified, `clean:generate:exports` = `rm -rf pkg/ts ...` deletes the export-manifest output ./pkg/ts/index.ts yet fails 5.1.4b, since cleanRemoves (:499-501) wants the literal file path, not a parent directory or glob. Loose as well: a generator output not listed in export.manifest.json (e.g. pkg/templates written by generate:templates) can be dropped from clean:generated and nothing fails. Fix: issue I-97.

Issues: I-21, I-97.

Any package with `generate:*` scripts also defines a
non-empty `generate` aggregate and a non-empty `clean:generated` deleting every file the generators write; the
reverse holds too — `generate` or `clean:generated` with no `generate:*` leaf is dead wiring and is rejected.

Wiring is checked by name: every `generate:*` leaf must be reachable from `generate` through same-package `npm run`
references (exempt: `generate:genesis`, a stateful anvil deploy, and `generate:patch-sites`, a committed baseline a
test compares against), and every `export.manifest.json` output must be deleted by `clean:generated`.

This exists because a regenerate-and-diff gate cannot see a generator that silently _stops_ emitting a file: the
committed copy sits untouched, so nothing looks dirty. Deleting first turns that into a visible deletion, and the
delete list lives beside the generators — the only place it stands a chance of being kept current.

```jsonc
// ✅ Every path the generate:* scripts write is removable, and one verb rewrites everything.
// (Here the export manifest names only pkg/ts/index.ts.)
"scripts": {
  "clean:generated": "rm -rf pkg/abi pkg/templates pkg/ts/index.ts",
  "generate": "npm run generate:exports && npm run generate:templates",
  "generate:exports": "node ../../fhevm-npm/fhevm-npm.ts generate exports ./export.manifest.json",
  "generate:templates": "node ./internal/cli/generateTemplates.ts"
}
```

```jsonc
// ❌ Generators with no way to prove they still emit everything.
"scripts": { "generate:exports": "node ../../fhevm-npm/fhevm-npm.ts generate exports ./export.manifest.json" }
```

## NR-43c: A package can delete its build output `[GAP]`

> A private source-owning package can delete its own build output.

Old number: 5.1.4c.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check scripts`

Evidence:

- Gap, wrong check: Compliant change that fails: remove `clean` from hardhat/v2/fhevm-hardhat-template/package.json, the dev owner of a mirror-only payload. The rule exempts it; scripts.ts:56 reports `package must define a non-empty 'clean' script` under the label package-scripts. Fix: issue I-98.

Issues: I-21, I-43, I-98.

Every `dev`, `shared-helper` and
`internal-consumer` package that is not a mirror owner defines a non-empty `clean`. Its content requirements are
derived from what the package actually does, never listed centrally:

- a package whose scripts invoke `tsc` must delete `*.tsbuildinfo`, because a surviving build-info file lets the
  next typecheck resume from stale state;
- a Forge project must delete the directories `forge config --json` reports (`cache_path`, `out`, `broadcast`).

Those directory names are **asked of forge, never assumed** — `hardhat/v2/e2e` sets `cache_path = "cache-forge"`, so
any rule hard-coding `cache` is already wrong for some projects. Anywhere this repo needs a Foundry answer,
`forge config --json` (which resolves `extends`, profiles and defaults) is the source, never a parsed `foundry.toml`.

```jsonc
// ✅ Derived from what the package does: it runs tsc, and forge reports cache/out/broadcast.
"scripts": {
  "clean": "rm -rf cache out broadcast *.tsbuildinfo pkg/ts/_esm pkg/ts/_cjs",
  "compile:forge": "forge build --skip test"
}
```

```jsonc
// ❌ A rebuild resumes from stale incremental state.
"scripts": { "clean": "rm -rf out", "lint": "eslint && tsc -p ./tsconfig.json --noEmit" }
```

## NR-44: Prettier does not format Solidity `[GAP]`

> Prettier scripts do not target Solidity.

Old number: 5.1.5.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check scripts`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: The check reads the text of the two scripts and does not follow npm run references. "prettier:check": "npm run prettier:all" with "prettier:all": "prettier --check \"**/*.{sol,ts}\"" passes. So does "prettier --check ." once a Solidity Prettier plugin is declared and added to prettier.base.mjs: no check reads the base's content or forbids the plugin. Fix: issue I-99.

Issues: I-42, I-99.

`forge fmt` is the sole Solidity formatter, so
`prettier:check` and `prettier:write` must exclude `.sol`. A mirror-only payload keeps its upstream Prettier setup
instead, the Solidity Prettier plugin and `.sol` in its Prettier scripts included, and does not require `forge:fmt`,
`forge:fmt:check` or `forge:lint` on its dev owner. The rendered mirror keeps Solhint on purpose: the mirror patch
does not remove it, so the published template keeps the Solhint upstream declares. The workspace form does not carry
it. In the workspace, [NR-20](../entries/NR-20.md) forbids the package unless the payload's manifest entry lists it in
`dependencyExceptions`, and no entry does; the banned-linter scan of `fhevm-npm check lint-policy` skips mirror-only
trees, so a Solhint configuration or directive there is not reported.

```jsonc
// ✅ Solidity is intentionally absent.
"prettier:check": "prettier --check \"**/*.{js,json,md,ts,yml}\""

// ❌ This gives Solidity two formatters with potentially different output.
"prettier:write": "prettier --write \"**/*.{js,json,md,sol,ts,yml}\""
```

## NR-45: Use the workspace Prettier configuration `[GAP]`

> A non-published package running Prettier uses the workspace configuration, unless it is a template under a `…-dev` owner.

Old number: 5.1.6.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check scripts`

Evidence:

- Gap, wrong check: Compliant change that fails: a trailing comment on the statement line, `export { default } from '../prettier.base.mjs'; // shared base`. withoutComments removes only block comments and whole-line `//` comments, so the anchored regex no longer matches and the check reports `must contain: export { default } ...`. The rule says comments are ignored, in every package. Fix: issue I-100.

Issues: I-01, I-100.

It contains `prettier.config.js` re-exporting the workspace root's `prettier.base.mjs` by relative
path; the only accepted config filenames are those two. A dev owner containing only `package.json` and `pkg/` has no
local source to format, so any local Prettier config is forbidden. An installation root carries neither. Two packages
are spared the re-export. A mirror-only payload's dev owner need not carry it. A package at `<owner>/pkg` whose parent
`<owner>` is an inventoried package whose name ends in `-dev`, such as a workspace-native template, contains its own
`prettier.config.js` instead: users receive that template on its own, so `fhevm-npm check scripts` fails
a Prettier or ESLint config in it that imports, by a literal specifier, a workspace-only package or a relative or
absolute path that resolves lexically outside it. The check is static: it does not see a computed import or a URI
specifier such as `file:`, and it does not follow symlinks, so it is no proof that the config is self-contained at run
time.

**The workspace root is the sole exception: it holds both, and both are required.** `prettier.base.mjs` is the shared
base, and `prettier.config.js` re-exports it. The second is not a duplicate: `prettier.base.mjs` is not a filename
Prettier discovers, so the files that sit directly in the workspace root and belong to no package — `npm-manifest.json`,
`cleartext-config.json`, the root-level docs — are formatted with the shared base only through that re-export. Two
configs are allowed here; two sources of formatting truth are not, so the re-export is pinned to the one statement.

Comments are ignored when the statement is pinned, in every package: prose explaining a config is not a fork of it.

```js
// ✅ In an ESM common/prettier.config.js.
export { default } from '../prettier.base.mjs';

// ✅ In a CommonJS package's prettier.config.js.
module.exports = import('../../../prettier.base.mjs').then((module) => module.default);

// ✅ At the workspace root, beside prettier.base.mjs, comment and all.
export { default } from './prettier.base.mjs';

// ✅ In a template at <owner>/pkg under a `…-dev` owner: self-contained, nothing imported from the workspace.
export default { singleQuote: true, printWidth: 120 };
```

```text
❌ Alternate configuration filename:
.prettierrc.mjs

❌ At the workspace root, restating options instead of re-exporting the base:
export default { singleQuote: true };
```

## NR-46: Three ESLint layers `[GAP]`

> ESLint configuration has three layers: policy, layout, local.

Old number: 5.1.7.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check scripts`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: on `release/0.14.x`, `fhevm-npm/base/checks/scripts.ts:840-843` checks only the ESLint filenames inside packages; nothing checks the layout layer. Fix: the `validateEslintLayoutModules` check (issue I-62), pushed on a branch, not yet merged.

Issues: I-01, I-09, I-11, I-62.

- **Policy:** the workspace root holds the one `eslint.base.mjs`. It sets which rules apply and at what severity,
  and names no package path.
- **Entry:** every non-published package that defines `lint` contains `eslint.config.js`. It is the only file
  ESLint loads, and the only ESLint config filename allowed in a package. A dev owner that contains only
  `package.json` and `pkg/` has no ESLint config.
- **Layout:** which directories get which rules. A package states its layout in its own `eslint.config.js`. When
  two or more packages share the same layout, it may live once in a shared module, `<family>/eslint.<name>.mjs`.
  The module sits in the common parent folder of those packages, outside every package. It imports
  `eslint.base.mjs`, gives paths only, sets no rule, and is imported by each `eslint.config.js` that uses it, all
  of them below its folder. It is `.mjs` because the nearest `package.json` declares no `type`.
- **Local:** what belongs to one package only stays in its `eslint.config.js`: its own ignores, and a rule turned
  off for named files, with a comment that says why.

```text
✅ eslint.base.mjs                        policy
   <family>/eslint.<name>.mjs            layout shared by <family>/<vN>
   <family>/<vN>/eslint.config.js        entry + local
❌ <family>/<vN>/eslint.layout.mjs        a layout module inside a package
❌ <family>/eslint.<name>.mjs             imported by one package only: inline it
❌ eslint.config.mjs, .eslintrc.json      not the entry filename
```
